lessons.title: Numbers 13–17
lessons.scenario: Smarty is at a birthday party and asks friends how old they are. Practise the numbers after twelve; ages can be imaginary.

items.note: Say thirteen when you count one more than twelve.
Say fourteen for the number after thirteen.
Say fifteen when you tell someone your age or count to fifteen.
Say sixteen to count sixteen things.
Say seventeen for the number after sixteen.

practice.prompt: Which word is the number 13?
practice.explanation: Thirteen is the number after twelve.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen to the number at the end: fourteen.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: Say I am and then your age.

practice.prompt: Ben has 16 apples. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Sixteen is the number 16.

practice.prompt: Match each number word to its number.
practice.explanation: Each word matches one number from 13 to 17.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if the microphone mishears you.
practice.explanation: You counted to seventeen out loud.

practice.prompt: Sam is 17 years old. Which sentence is right?
practice.explanation: Seventeen is the number 17.

practice.prompt: Listen to the question, then choose a good reply.
practice.explanation: How old are you? asks for your age, so give a number and years old.

practice.prompt: Which word comes after twelve?
practice.explanation: Twelve, then thirteen. Eleven comes before twelve.

story.hook: Everyone at the party says an age. Who is the oldest?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hello! How old are you, Mia?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I am thirteen years old.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And you, Sam?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I am fourteen. Ben is fifteen.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Ana is sixteen. Leo is seventeen.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Thank you, Ben!

questions.explanation: Mia says: I am thirteen years old.
Sam says: Ben is fifteen.
Ben says: Leo is seventeen. Ana is sixteen.

image.describe: A birthday party in a garden with balloons; Smarty the black cat, Mia, Sam, Ben, Ana and Leo stand around a cake, with no written words or numbers.

mission.setup: Smarty asks your age and a friend's age at the party. Use an imaginary age if you like.

turns.smarty: How old are you?
turns.hint: Say I am and a number from eleven to seventeen.

turns.smarty: Mia is thirteen. And your friend?
turns.hint: Say a friend's name or He is / She is, and an age.

lessons.title: Numbers to 50
lessons.scenario: Smarty and friends count apples, bananas and eggs in the boxes. Practise bigger numbers up to fifty.

items.note: Say eighteen for the number after seventeen.
Say nineteen for the number just before twenty.

items.example: There are thirty apples in the box.
items.note: Say thirty for 30; it is a different word from thirteen.

items.example: My father is forty years old.
items.note: Say forty for 40; after twenty and thirty comes forty.

items.example: There are fifty books on the table.
items.note: Say fifty for 50, and add a small number after it to count on.

practice.prompt: Which word is the number 30?
practice.explanation: Thirty is 30. Thirteen is 13, a much smaller number.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Nineteen is the last number before twenty.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: There are comes first, then the number, then the thing you count.

practice.prompt: My father is 50 years old. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Fifty is the number 50.

practice.prompt: Match each number word to its number.
practice.explanation: Each word matches one number.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if the microphone mishears you.
practice.explanation: You said a number just before twenty.

practice.prompt: Which word comes after seventeen?
practice.explanation: Seventeen, then eighteen.

practice.prompt: Count in tens: ten, twenty, ... Which word comes next?
practice.explanation: Count in tens: ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Sixteen ends with -teen. Listen to the end of the word.

story.hook: The friends count what is in the boxes. How many are there?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Look, Smarty! There are thirty apples.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Great, Sam! And there are forty bananas.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: There are fifty oranges in the box.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I have eighteen eggs.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: I have nineteen cups.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Thank you, Sam!

questions.explanation: Sam says: There are thirty apples.
Ben says: I have eighteen eggs.

questions.prompt: How many oranges are in the box?
questions.explanation: Mia says: There are fifty oranges in the box.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat, Sam, Mia, Ben and Ana stand around open wooden boxes full of apples, bananas and oranges on a table, with no written words or numbers.

mission.setup: Smarty is counting boxes and asks about ages and apples. Use bigger numbers; imaginary numbers are fine.

turns.smarty: How old is your father?
turns.hint: Say He is and a number, for example forty.

turns.smarty: I have nineteen apples. And you?
turns.hint: Say I have and a number, then apples.

lessons.title: Numbers to 100
lessons.scenario: Friends tell Smarty the ages in their families. Practise counting in tens all the way to one hundred.

items.example: My father is sixty years old.
items.note: Say sixty for 60; it comes after fifty.
Say seventy for 70; after sixty comes seventy.

items.example: My grandmother is eighty years old.
items.note: Say eighty for 80; the ending sounds like eight.

items.example: My grandfather is ninety years old.
items.note: Say ninety for 90, and do not mix it up with nineteen.
Say one hundred for 100; it is the biggest number you can count to in this unit.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat sitting next to a huge pile of one hundred shiny coins; the picture has no written words or digits.

practice.prompt: Which word is the number 60?
practice.explanation: Sixty is 60. Sixteen is a smaller number.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: My grandmother is eighty years old.
practice.answer: My grandmother is eighty years old.
options: My grandmother is eighty years old.
My grandmother is seventy years old.
My grandmother is ninety years old.
practice.explanation: Listen for eighty. It sounds like eight.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: Say one hundred together: one, then hundred.

practice.prompt: There are 90 apples in the box. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: There are ___ apples in the box.
practice.explanation: Ninety is 90. Nineteen is only 19.

practice.prompt: Match each number word to its number.
practice.explanation: Each word matches one number, up to one hundred.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if the microphone mishears you.
practice.explanation: You said ninety. Try to hear the difference from nineteen.

practice.prompt: Which comes after ninety?
practice.explanation: Ninety, then one hundred.

practice.prompt: Count in tens: fifty, sixty, ... Which word comes next?
practice.explanation: Count in tens: fifty, sixty, seventy.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Forty ends with -ty. Fourteen ends with -teen.

practice.prompt: You are 13. Complete the sentence about your age.
practice.explanation: Thirteen is 13. Thirty is 30.

story.hook: Who has the biggest number of all?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: How old is your grandmother, Mia?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: She is eighty years old.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: My grandfather is ninety years old.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: My mother is sixty. My father is seventy.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Great! And I have one hundred apples.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Smarty, you have one hundred apples?

questions.explanation: Mia says: She is eighty years old.

questions.prompt: Who has a grandfather that is ninety?
questions.explanation: Sam says: My grandfather is ninety years old.
Smarty says: I have one hundred apples.

image.describe: A sunny school garden where Smarty the black cat, Mia, Sam and Ben sit on a bench and talk; behind them a stall with a pile of apples, no written words or numbers.

mission.setup: Smarty talks about family ages and apples. Imaginary ages and answers are fine.

turns.smarty: How old is your grandmother?
accept: ^(?:she is|my grandmother is|grandma is) (?:forty|fifty|sixty|seventy|eighty|ninety)(?: years old)?$
turns.hint: Say She is and a number such as seventy or eighty.

turns.smarty: I have one hundred apples. Do you like apples?
accept: ^no(?: i do not| i do not like apples)?$
turns.hint: Answer Yes or No. You can add I like apples.

lessons.title: How much is it?
lessons.scenario: You visit Smarty's little shop and ask what things cost. Practise asking the price and saying a price is low.

items.note: Ask "How much is it?" when you want to know the price.
Money is what you give in a shop to buy something.

image.describe: A small pile of coins and plain paper notes on a wooden table beside Smarty the black cat; there are no digits or words on them.

items.note: Use dollar after a number to say a price; with more than one, say dollars.

image.describe: Mia holding up one plain green paper bill with a happy face; the bill has no digits or words on it.

items.note: Say cheap when the price is low.

practice.prompt: You want to know the price. What do you ask?
practice.explanation: How much is it? asks about the price.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: How much asks the price. What time asks the clock.

practice.prompt: Build the answer about the price.
practice.explanation: It is, then the number, then dollars.

practice.prompt: The bread is only one dollar. Choose the word for a low price.
practice.explanation: Cheap means the price is low.

practice.prompt: Match each question to a good reply.
practice.explanation: Each question needs its own kind of answer: a price, a time or an age.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if the microphone mishears you.
practice.explanation: You asked the price out loud.

practice.prompt: Which word is for coins and paper notes?
practice.explanation: Money is what you pay with.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Twenty is 20. Twelve is 12.

practice.prompt: Ask for bread politely.
practice.explanation: Can I have ... , please? is a polite way to ask.

practice.prompt: Build the question about the apple.
practice.explanation: How much is ... ? works with any thing you want to buy.

Mia says: I have money.

questions.explanation: Mia asks: Can I have two apples, please?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat behind the counter of a little shop with a loaf of bread and a basket of apples; Mia stands in front of the counter holding some coins, no written words or numbers.

mission.setup: You are a customer in Smarty's little shop. Ask the price and say what you think of it.

turns.smarty: Hello! Look, we have bread, milk and apples.
turns.hint: Ask the price with How much is it?

turns.smarty: It is three dollars.
turns.hint: Say it is cheap, thank Smarty, or ask Can I have it, please?

lessons.title: It's expensive
lessons.scenario: You and Sam look at things in Smarty's shop. Talk about prices and decide what to buy.

items.note: Say expensive when the price is high.
Price is the number of dollars a thing costs.

image.describe: A blank paper price tag hanging on a red apple, with Smarty the black cat looking at it; the tag has no digits or words.

items.note: A shop is the place where you buy things.

image.describe: The front of a little shop with a striped awning and shelves of apples and bread, with Smarty the black cat standing in the doorway.

items.note: Use buy when you give money and get something.

practice.prompt: A coat is one hundred dollars. Which word describes the price?
practice.explanation: A very high price is expensive.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the thing and the price word.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: I want to buy + the thing you want.

practice.prompt: Where do you buy apples? Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: You buy things in a shop.

practice.prompt: Match the word to the idea.
practice.explanation: Expensive goes with a high price, cheap with a low price, and a shop sells food.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if the microphone mishears you.
practice.explanation: You told someone the price.

practice.prompt: Which question asks about the price?
practice.explanation: How much is it? asks about the price.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Money is what you use in a shop.

practice.prompt: You want to know the price. Complete the question.
practice.explanation: How much asks about the price.

practice.prompt: Someone asks: How much is it? Choose the answer.
practice.explanation: A price answer uses dollars.

story.hook: Sam sees a jacket and a hat. Which one can he buy?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Hello, Smarty! Is this jacket cheap?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: No, it is expensive. The price is fifty dollars.

lines.text: I have thirty dollars.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Thank you, Sam!

questions.explanation: Smarty says: The price is fifty dollars.

questions.prompt: What does Sam want to buy?

turns.smarty: This hat is ten dollars. Do you want to buy it?
turns.example: Yes, I want to buy it.
turns.hint: Say Yes or No. You can add I want to buy it.

lessons.title: At the market
lessons.scenario: You and Ana shop at the market. Ask for food, say how many, and ask for kilos and bottles.

items.example: I buy tomatoes at the market.
items.note: A market is a place with many stalls where you buy food.

image.describe: A busy open-air market with colourful fruit and vegetable stalls under bright umbrellas; Smarty the black cat walks between the stalls.

items.example: I want one kilo of apples.
items.note: Use kilo to say how much food you want.

image.describe: A kitchen scale with a pile of red apples on it and Mia watching; the scale has no numbers or words.

items.note: Use How many to ask the number of things.

items.example: I want a bottle of water.
items.note: Use bottle for water, milk or juice.

image.describe: A clear glass bottle of water standing on a wooden table next to a cup.

practice.prompt: You want to ask about the number of apples. What do you ask?
practice.explanation: How many asks about the number of things.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.

practice.answer: I want one kilo of apples.

I want one kilo of tomatoes.

practice.explanation: Kilos is for food that you weigh.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if the microphone mishears you.
practice.explanation: You asked about the number of apples.

practice.prompt: Someone asks: How many apples? Choose the answer.

lessons.title: I'd like this one
lessons.scenario: Lily chooses things in Smarty's shop. Say what you would like and point to this one or that one.

items.note: Say I would like when you want to ask for something politely.
Say this one for a thing that is near you.
Say that one for a thing that is far from you.

items.example: The apples are in the basket.
items.note: A basket holds the things you want to buy.

image.describe: A woven basket full of red apples and a loaf of bread standing on a shop counter.

practice.answer: I would like a cake, please.
options: I would like a cake, please.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I would like this one, please.
practice.answer: I would like this one, please.
options: I would like this one, please.
I would like that one, please.
practice.explanation: This one is near you, and that one is far.

lessons.title: Smarty's shop
lessons.canDo: Serve a customer in Smarty's shop
lessons.scenario: It is a busy day in Smarty's little shop. Welcome a customer, offer help, ask about anything else and say the price.

items.note: Say "Can I help you?" when a customer comes into your shop.
Say "Just looking" when you want to look first and not buy yet.
Ask "Anything else?" when a customer wants more things.
Say "That is all" when you do not want any more things.

practice.prompt: You walk into a shop. The assistant speaks first. What does the assistant say?
practice.explanation: Can I help you? is the usual start in a shop.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Just looking means you do not want to buy yet.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: That is all, thank you ends your order politely.

practice.prompt: The assistant wants to know if you want more things. Complete the question.
practice.explanation: Anything else? asks if you want more.

practice.prompt: Match each question to a good reply.
practice.explanation: Each question in a shop has a short, polite reply.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if the microphone mishears you.
practice.explanation: You welcomed a customer.

practice.prompt: You want to know how the customer will pay. What do you ask?
practice.explanation: Card or cash? asks how the customer will pay.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I would like that one, please.
practice.answer: I would like that one, please.
options: I would like this one, please.
I would like that one, please.
practice.explanation: That one is far from you; this one is near.

practice.prompt: Someone asks: How much is it? Choose the answer.
practice.explanation: A price answer uses dollars.

practice.prompt: You want apples. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I would like two kilos of ___.
practice.explanation: You buy apples by the kilo.

story.hook: A customer says Just looking. Will she buy something?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Good morning! Can I help you?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Just looking, thank you.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Sorry, Smarty. I would like this bottle of juice.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Of course! Anything else?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Two apples, please. That is all.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: It is five dollars. Card or cash?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Card, please. Here you are.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Thank you, Mia! Goodbye!

questions.explanation: Mia first says: Just looking, thank you.
Mia wants a bottle of juice and two apples.
Mia says: Card, please.

image.describe: Inside Smarty's little shop, Smarty the black cat in an apron serves Mia at the counter; juice bottles, apples and bread are on the shelves behind, no written words or numbers.

mission.setup: You are the shop assistant in Smarty's little shop. Smarty is the customer. Welcome him, offer more, and say the price.
